midnight_rule: Hour 24 closes the narrative day; the world calendar has advanced to the next day.

broadcasts.title: Morning weather
broadcasts.text: Good morning. This is North Ridge Public Radio at six. The regional forecast calls for a cold morning and changeable cloud through the afternoon. Carry winter clothing and allow extra time on the logging roads. Schools, the clinic and local deliveries are operating normally. We will have another bulletin at noon.

broadcasts.title: Midday recap
broadcasts.text: It is noon on North Ridge Public Radio. A recap of this morning: cold weather remains the main concern for northern travellers. Dress warmly and check road conditions before leaving town. The clinic and local services remain open, and regular deliveries are expected. Our next bulletin is at five this afternoon.

broadcasts.title: Distant incidents
broadcasts.text: This is the five o'clock bulletin. Authorities on the other side of the country are investigating several violent incidents at hospitals and transit stations. Officials have not established whether the reports are connected. There are no confirmed local incidents in North Ridge. Avoid sharing unverified claims. We will update the story at midnight.

broadcasts.title: First overnight update
broadcasts.text: It is midnight. Reports of violent attacks now involve several cities. Hospitals in the affected areas are restricting access, and some emergency crews have stopped answering calls. Officials still dispute the cause. No evacuation order has been issued here. Keep your radio available. We will return at six in the morning.

broadcasts.title: Regional precautions
broadcasts.text: Good morning from North Ridge. The forecast remains cold. Overnight disturbances have spread into our region. The clinic is screening arrivals at its side entrance, and police ask residents to avoid crowds and unnecessary travel. The cause remains unconfirmed. Keep essential supplies at home. At noon we will recap the confirmed information.

broadcasts.title: Regional midday recap
broadcasts.text: It is noon. A recap of this morning's bulletin: regional hospitals are restricting access after reports of violent behaviour. Police advise avoiding crowds and unnecessary journeys. Do not approach injured strangers behaving aggressively. The cause is still under investigation. North Ridge deliveries may be delayed. We will carry further confirmed reports at five.

broadcasts.title: Town disruption
broadcasts.text: This is the five o'clock bulletin. There have been attacks on responders near the North Ridge clinic and the western town junction. Several roads into town are closed. Shops are shutting early and fuel deliveries have been suspended. Stay clear of the clinic and roadblocks. This station is checking reports with the remaining emergency crews.

broadcasts.title: Unexplained deaths
broadcasts.text: It is midnight. Responders describe people moving again after injuries they believed were fatal. Those accounts have not been independently verified, but the attacks are real. The clinic cannot accept further patients. Residents should remain indoors where possible, secure entrances, and prepare drinking water, food and heating fuel. Our next scheduled report is at six.

broadcasts.title: Shelter advisory
broadcasts.text: Good morning. Multiple emergency teams now confirm that some of the dead are rising and attacking the living. Avoid close contact with anyone showing aggressive or disoriented behaviour. North Ridge residents should shelter where they can. Electrical service is becoming unreliable across the region. Fill clean containers with water and keep a safe source of heat ready.

broadcasts.title: Shelter midday recap
broadcasts.text: It is noon. This morning's advice remains in force: avoid close contact with the infected, secure your shelter, and prepare water, food and heating fuel. Reports of the dead rising have been confirmed by several emergency teams. Electrical failures are spreading. A repaired local installation cannot restore the regional network. Travel only when your supplies require it.

broadcasts.title: Northern isolation
broadcasts.text: This is the five o'clock bulletin. Emergency assistance cannot reach the northern logging roads. The town centre is unsafe, and regular deliveries have stopped. Choose a route before travelling. Move in daylight, keep away from crowds, and return with enough water and fuel to remain sheltered. This transmitter has reserve power, but our outside reports are becoming scarce.

broadcasts.title: No relief convoy
broadcasts.text: It is midnight. No relief convoy has reached North Ridge. Several communities are no longer answering radio checks. Do not leave a defensible shelter simply because you expect collection. Treat water, protect wounds and conserve medical supplies. We will continue the scheduled bulletins while this station can operate. The next is at six.

broadcasts.title: Independent survival
broadcasts.text: Good morning. There is no reliable regional power or emergency service. Overnight reports place infected groups on roads into and through town. Keep enough fuel to stay warm after dark. If you must seek supplies, plan your return before setting out. This station cannot promise rescue. Our noon bulletin will repeat the practical advice we can still verify.

broadcasts.title: Independent survival recap
broadcasts.text: It is noon. A recap of this morning's advice: assume help and regular deliveries are unavailable. Maintain your shelter, treat drinking water, and keep dry heating fuel in reserve. Infected groups have been reported along the town approaches. Travel with a return route and leave room to carry useful supplies. Do not spend your final reserves waiting for rescue.

broadcasts.title: Shrinking information
broadcasts.text: This is the five o'clock bulletin. We have fewer working contacts and cannot verify the condition of every road. Silence from a community does not mean that it is safe. Store doors, clinic grounds and traffic queues remain dangerous places to linger. There will be no scheduled supply deliveries. Concentrate on water, warmth and a defensible place to rest.

broadcasts.title: Station reserve warning
broadcasts.text: It is midnight. The station is operating on its remaining reserve. We can still announce the scheduled bulletins, but there are no dependable outside services behind them. Keep your local equipment working and conserve what you have. A familiar voice on the radio is not a promise that somebody can reach you. We return at six.

broadcasts.title: Final operating day
broadcasts.text: Good morning from North Ridge. This is expected to be our final day of scheduled broadcasting. Our reserve power is nearly exhausted. There is still no confirmed relief operation for the northern communities. Maintain water, warmth and food before considering another journey. We intend to return at noon, five, and midnight if the transmitter holds.

broadcasts.title: Final midday recap
broadcasts.text: It is noon. This morning's notice remains unchanged: today is expected to be the final operating day for this station. No relief service has been confirmed. Conserve medical supplies, keep drinking water safe, and prepare your shelter for another cold night. We intend to make the five o'clock report and a final midnight signoff.

broadcasts.title: Preparing for silence
broadcasts.text: This is the five o'clock bulletin. We have no new verified outside reports. The transmitter has enough reserve for the planned midnight signoff. Do not treat the silence afterwards as an all clear. Continue the precautions you already know. Keep a route home, keep dry fuel, and help the people you can reach without abandoning your own shelter.

broadcasts.title: Final signoff
broadcasts.text: It is midnight. This is North Ridge Public Radio's final scheduled transmission. Our reserve is exhausted. No further bulletin will follow at six. If you are listening, keep your shelter secure, your water clean and your people warm. Remember that you have already survived days without dependable help. Take care of each other. North Ridge signing off.

broadcasts.title: Assignment check
broadcasts.text: Kestrel Seven, dispatch. Your personal receiver is coming through clearly. Inspect the transfer cabinet if you have not already done so. A replacement relay was reserved at North Ridge Supply. Keep the standby battery charged and read your desk log before travelling. We will check in later.

broadcasts.title: Afternoon work check
broadcasts.text: Kestrel Seven, dispatch checking in. If you still need the replacement relay, it was reserved at North Ridge Supply. The desk public radio carries the regional bulletins; this handset stays with you for work calls. Take the logging track down to the road and keep enough daylight for the return. If the job is finished, keep the installation on standby.

broadcasts.title: End of shift
broadcasts.text: Kestrel Seven, last work check tonight. We have heard the distant reports, but no change to your assignment has been confirmed. Stay at the lookout overnight if you can. Keep the stove supplied and leave your local battery charged. The next routine dispatch call is in the morning.

broadcasts.title: Travel precautions
broadcasts.text: Kestrel Seven, dispatch. The situation has reached our region. Avoid the clinic and any gathering near the town junction. If you still need the reserved part, take what you need and return before dark. Keep this handset on you. Your desk radio is the public news source, not this work channel.

broadcasts.title: Delivery cancelled
broadcasts.text: Kestrel Seven, the supply truck will not reach your site. Do not wait on the road for it. Keep your provisions and use the lookout as your base. If your relay is already commissioned, preserve the backup charge. We cannot promise a replacement crew or another delivery.

broadcasts.title: Town crew missing
broadcasts.text: Kestrel Seven, dispatch. We have lost contact with the town crew. The last confirmed report placed them near the western junction. Do not go looking for them without a safe return route. Secure your shelter and gather supplies only when you need them. We will try another call in the morning.

broadcasts.title: Working independently
broadcasts.text: Kestrel Seven, dispatch. We cannot send anyone to your site. Keep your water, heating fuel and food in reserve. Your installation only supports local equipment; repairing it cannot bring the town network back. Check the public station at its scheduled times if your desk receiver still has power.

broadcasts.title: Conserve local power
broadcasts.text: Kestrel Seven, a short check. If the mains have failed, turn off the desk lamp when you do not need it and conserve the local battery. Your personal handset has its own supply and receives our calls directly. Do not exhaust your heating fuel trying to finish every job. Shelter and water come first.

broadcasts.title: Dispatch thinning out
broadcasts.text: Kestrel Seven, dispatch. There are very few of us left answering this net. Keep treating water and securing your shelter. The town cannot be relied on for regular supplies. If you travel, choose the return route first and leave room in your pack. We will attempt one more morning check.

broadcasts.title: Last dispatch call
broadcasts.text: Kestrel Seven, this may be our last call. We cannot maintain the dispatch net. You are released from the assignment. Use the lookout, the tools and the supplies you can recover to keep yourself alive. The public station is independent and may still be broadcasting. Do not wait for us. Dispatch out.
